samples.question: The picture shows a grey corridor running left to right, with a black triangle at the far left: that is a courier, and the grey arrow in the top margin shows that the courier walks from left to right. Standing along the corridor is a row of coloured objects of exactly two shapes. A small coloured disc, drawn above the corridor on a short grey stem, is a key lying on a shelf: when the courier reaches it, the courier picks it up and adds one key of that disc's colour to the bag it carries. A tall coloured post, drawn standing across the corridor itself, is a locked gate: to walk past it the courier must hand over one key of that gate's own colour, and that key is used up and leaves the bag for good. Keys are not interchangeable between colours and there is no other way through a gate. The bag starts empty, keys of the same colour pile up, and the courier meets the discs and posts one at a time in the order they are drawn from left to right. If the courier reaches a gate while holding no key of that gate's colour, the courier is stopped there and walks no further, so everything drawn to the right of that gate is never reached. Exactly one gate stops the courier in every picture. The bag's contents are never drawn anywhere: only the discs and posts standing in the corridor are drawn, and a disc stays drawn whether or not its key has already been spent. What is the colour of the gate that stops the courier? Answer with one of blue, green, orange, purple or yellow.
